subject: SI enablement & certification roadmap for Nordic + Japan (data residency constraints)
messages:
From: Anna Lindqvist <anna@nordiclogic.se>

Date: 2026-07-29T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Regional SI enablement: Nordic & Japan data residency

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the intro at the cloud forum last week — curious to explore a formal enablement path for NordicLogic as a Redwood SI in the Nordics and for our Tokyo partner affiliates. Two constraints we heard repeatedly from prospects: (1) strict EU data residency requirements for customer data (they want data to remain in EU regions and audit trails accessible locally) and (2) in Japan many customers ask for local certifications / government attestation (ISMAP, local KMS integration).

Can you share a recommended checklist / timeline for certifying a regional SI (technical, legal, and commercial checkpoints)? We'd like to align on a mutual action plan and an estimated time-to-market for a certified SI offering in both regions.

Appreciate any templates or examples you can share.

Best,
Anna
Head of Cloud Partnerships
NordicLogic

Hi Anna — great to hear from you and glad the forum sparked this. Outline below is a pragmatic roadmap we've used with other SIs; I attached a certification checklist and a first-draft mutual action plan (MAP_Nordic_JP_v1.xlsx).

High-level steps we recommend:
- Legal & procurement: NDA -> Partner Addendum (data residency clauses, SOC2 / ISMAP equivalence)
- Technical: private deployment options (VPC connector, private control plane), KMS/HSM integration, regional peering & network topology validation
- Security evidence: SOC2 reports, pen-test summaries, architecture diagrams (we'll provide redacted evidence for partner review)
- Enablement: joint technical workshop, runbook for prefix caching and quantization settings per workload, POC baseline tests (latency & throughput targets)
- Go-to-market: co-sell materials, pricing guidance for dedicated instances, support SLAs and escalation playbook

Proposed timeline (ballpark): 4–8 weeks for EU readiness if legal redlines are minimal; 6–10+ weeks for JP depending on ISMAP mapping and local KMS integrations.

Next steps: can we set a 45-minute working session next week (tech + legal) to align scope and owners?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
Marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: cert-checklist-v2.pdf; MAP_Nordic_JP_v1.xlsx

Anna / team — quick legal note to flag items we'll need to surface early:

1) Data flow diagrams for each deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private) — callers, control plane locations, audit log retention locations
2) KMS ownership model — who holds keys, HSM/KMS region mapping, and whether we need customer-managed keys (CMK) by region
3) Cross-border transfer consents and DPA language (for EU: SCCs + any Schrems II mitigations; for JP: ISMAP mapping and local retention requirements)
4) Evidence list: redacted SOC2, latest pen-test summary, RBAC & SSO integration docs

I'll prepare a partner-ready DPA addendum template and a checklist (see attached cert-checklist-v2.pdf). Marissa — once we agree scope, I recommend a single shared Drive folder for evidence exchange (we can redact the parts that are sensitive).

Soojin

Thanks Marissa and Soojin. A few Japan-specific notes from our platform team:
- ISMAP alignment is the primary ask for some enterprise customers; we can map Redwood artifacts to ISMAP domains but will need the SOC2 assertion and architecture diagrams to build the mapping
- Many large customers expect local key residency (KMS in JP region) and sometimes on-prem HSM; can Redwood support CMK + customer-managed HSM in Dedicated/Private modes?
- Network: customers ask for local peering and predictable egress patterns for latency-sensitive inference; a plain diagram of expected peering points helps procurement.

We're happy to coordinate with your infra team during the technical workshop. Proposed agenda: 1) Architecture mapping (30m) 2) KMS options + key lifecycle (20m) 3) POC success criteria and perf targets (20m)

—Kenji
